item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-ec98a78a77a399c1","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"The World Bank reported that Egypt’s inflation reached 38% in late 2023 and that poverty increased by about five percentage points between 2022 and 2024; it also described fiscal and structural reforms as ongoing responses to macroeconomic vulnerabilities.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The inflation peak falls within 2023; the poverty comparison extends beyond the target period.","ruler_attribution":"The World Bank described government reforms and macroeconomic conditions under Egypt’s authorities; direct personal attribution to el-Sisi is not established.","limitations":["The page is current and includes post-2023 data.","No 2023 budget execution detail is provided."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ec98a78a77a399c1","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"World Bank-supported projects included emergency food-security measures from December 2022 to February 2023 that addressed wheat-import shortfalls and maintained uninterrupted bread subsidies; other projects supported social protection, housing, health, education, rail safety, and local infrastructure.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.9","6B.2","6B.6","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The food-security intervention directly covers the target period; other projects began earlier and continued beyond 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes implementation to the Government of Egypt with World Bank financing and technical support; it does not isolate el-Sisi’s personal decisions.","limitations":["External financing and World Bank implementation support complicate attribution.","Reported outputs are not limited to 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ec98a78a77a399c1","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"The World Bank reported that the Universal Health Insurance program had enrolled more than 5 million people in six phase-one governorates and that 322 providers had been accredited and contracted.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.4","6B.9","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The program was active during 2023, although the reported cumulative figures are not dated specifically to year-end 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The program was implemented by Egyptian authorities under the 2018 Universal Health Insurance Law with World Bank support.","limitations":["The source does not provide 2023-only enrollment or service-quality outcomes.","Attribution is shared with international financing and implementation partners."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6c54f76d034c96b9","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"The joint UPR submission stated that Egypt’s restrictions on expression and association remained in place and that authorities used repressive laws and prosecutions against human rights defenders, journalists, and activists.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The submission was filed in 2024 and published in 2025, but describes conditions and cases during and through 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The submission attributes the laws and practices to Egyptian government authorities under el-Sisi’s presidency.","limitations":["This is an advocacy submission by civil-society organizations.","Some cited laws predate 2023, though their implementation continued during the period."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6c54f76d034c96b9","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"In March 2023, journalists from Mada Masr were indicted on charges including spreading false information and misuse of communications; the editor-in-chief also faced pending cybercrime-related licensing charges. More than 600 websites, including news and human-rights sites, remained blocked, and several sites were blocked during 2023.","question_ids":["3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The indictments and website blocking described include events occurring in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The submission attributes the prosecutions and blocking to Egyptian authorities.","limitations":["The source reports allegations and legal proceedings rather than final judicial findings for every case.","The exact presidential chain of command is not documented."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6c54f76d034c96b9","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"In March 2023, an Emergency State Security Court sentenced four leaders of the Egyptian Coordination for Rights and Freedoms to five-to-fifteen-year prison terms, followed by police probation, terrorist-list designation, and closure of the organization’s website and social-media accounts.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.4","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The sentences and related measures occurred in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The submission attributes the prosecutions and sanctions to Egyptian authorities and emergency-state-security institutions.","limitations":["The source characterizes the charges as politically motivated and bogus; the court’s reasoning is not supplied.","Direct presidential authorization is not shown."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6c54f76d034c96b9","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The submission reported that on 11 May 2023 security forces abducted student activist Moaz al-Sharqawi, kept his location unknown for 29 days, and then brought terrorism charges against him.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The abduction and subsequent proceedings occurred in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The submission attributes the conduct to Egyptian security forces and the Supreme State Security Prosecution.","limitations":["The account comes from a civil-society submission.","No direct order from el-Sisi is documented."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6c54f76d034c96b9","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The submission reported that in August 2023 security forces raided journalist Karim Asaad’s home after corruption reports concerning the government, assaulted him and his wife, deleted two posts from the media platform, seized devices, and held him for two days with alleged physical and psychological abuse.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The incident occurred in August 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The submission attributes the raid to Egyptian security forces and links its timing to reporting implicating government actors.","limitations":["The allegations are reported by civil-society organizations and were not adjudicated in the supplied text.","Personal authorization by el-Sisi is not established."]},{"source_id":"SRC-98af5b2cb9870f83","start_unit":14,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that Egypt had not amended its penal-code definition of torture to conform to the Convention Against Torture and that article 129 allowed penalties as low as one year’s imprisonment or a fine for cruel treatment by officials.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","3B.9","7B.2"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The submission covers 2013 through mid-2023 and was published in October 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The legal framework remained in force under el-Sisi’s government.","limitations":["Human Rights Watch is an external rights monitor.","The source does not establish why no amendment was enacted."]},{"source_id":"SRC-98af5b2cb9870f83","start_unit":15,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch documented widespread and systematic torture by regular police and the National Security Agency in political cases, including beatings, electric shocks, stress positions, sexual assault, and coerced confessions, with prosecutors often ignoring complaints.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The documented cases and pattern extend through 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Human Rights Watch described the practices as occurring under el-Sisi’s government and involving Interior Ministry and National Security personnel.","limitations":["The source is a rights-monitoring submission and does not prove personal involvement in each incident.","The evidence base combines cases from multiple years."]},{"source_id":"SRC-98af5b2cb9870f83","start_unit":17,"end_unit":18,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported that prison overcrowding and inadequate medical care were systematic, that independent oversight was limited, and that authorities denied or rejected most requests by independent organizations and UN mandate holders to visit detention sites.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","6B.2","6B.5"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The submission describes conditions continuing through mid-2023.","ruler_attribution":"The practices are attributed to Egyptian authorities under el-Sisi’s government.","limitations":["The source relies on interviews, prior research, and reported access restrictions.","The supplied document does not provide a complete 2023 prison census."]},{"source_id":"SRC-98af5b2cb9870f83","start_unit":21,"end_unit":21,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported a 2023 case in which a transgender woman held in Egypt said she was raped more than 100 times during 290 days in detention, including 22 times in the first 15 days, and was denied adequate food.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.7","3B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The case was documented in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The alleged conduct involved Egyptian police and detention authorities under el-Sisi’s government.","limitations":["The account is a survivor allegation reported by Human Rights Watch.","No final judicial finding is supplied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-53abb31a44ba4d1e","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"Egypt’s 2023 reply to the Committee Against Torture stated that its National Human Rights Strategy, launched in 2021, addressed civil and political rights, abolition of the state of emergency, community correctional centers, and increased conditional releases and pardons.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.9","4B.3","8B.1","8B.2"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The reply was received in September 2023 and describes policies active during the target period.","ruler_attribution":"The Egyptian government presented these as executive and institutional policies under el-Sisi’s presidency.","limitations":["This is the government’s own submission and is contradicted by supplied external assessments.","The statement describes commitments and institutional measures more than independently verified outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-53abb31a44ba4d1e","start_unit":10,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that from November 2019 to May 2023 disciplinary or legal measures were taken in incidents involving 769 Interior Ministry employees; 380 were found to have violated the law, including cases involving cruelty, unlawful detention, ill-treatment, torture, and excessive force.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.4","3B.9","8B.8"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The figures include conduct and measures through May 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The reply attributes the disciplinary process to Interior Ministry and judicial authorities.","limitations":["The government does not identify the cases or publish independent verification.","Most cases were suspended or pending, and the figures do not demonstrate deterrence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-53abb31a44ba4d1e","start_unit":12,"end_unit":13,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that between 2019 and June 2023 the Public Prosecutor held 29 anti-trafficking training courses for 577 staff, while the Interior Ministry held 55 related courses in cooperation with international organizations.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.7","8B.3","8B.4","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The reported training period includes 2023 through June.","ruler_attribution":"The measures were implemented by the Public Prosecutor and Interior Ministry under the Egyptian government.","limitations":["Training attendance is an input and does not establish improved outcomes.","The figures are self-reported by the government."]},{"source_id":"SRC-53abb31a44ba4d1e","start_unit":13,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that its anti-trafficking policy used prevention, protection, prosecution, and international partnership; it launched a 2022–2026 national strategy, assigned eight judicial departments to trafficking cases, and established victim referral, shelter, legal-aid, and rehabilitation mechanisms.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.2","6B.3","6B.9","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The strategy and mechanisms were active during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The measures were attributed to Egyptian ministries, prosecutors, courts, and the national coordinating committee.","limitations":["The source provides limited independent evidence of actual access or outcomes for victims.","The policy concerns trafficking specifically rather than general domestic safety."]},{"source_id":"SRC-53abb31a44ba4d1e","start_unit":16,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that from January 2019 to June 2023 the Interior Ministry conducted 47 human-rights training courses, while the Public Prosecutor conducted 16 courses for 257 trainees; it also reported 22 human-rights courses in military colleges.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.4","8B.3","8B.4"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The reported activities include the target period through June 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The measures were presented as government programs of the Interior Ministry, Public Prosecutor, and Ministry of Defence.","limitations":["Training activity does not establish effective prevention or accountability.","The government’s figures are not independently audited in the source."]},{"source_id":"SRC-53abb31a44ba4d1e","start_unit":22,"end_unit":23,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that counter-terrorism operations after 2013 brought attacks under control and that no exceptional arrest, search, pretrial-detention, or trial measures beyond statutory law were used.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.6","3B.9","8B.7","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The government described a continuing policy and security outcome relevant to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The claim concerns counter-terrorism operations under the Egyptian government and security institutions.","limitations":["The claim is contested by the supplied Human Rights Watch and EIPR materials.","No quantitative violence trend or independent verification is supplied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-53abb31a44ba4d1e","start_unit":25,"end_unit":26,"fact_summary":"Egypt reported that from November 2019 to May 2023 measures were taken in cases involving 769 Interior Ministry employees, with 380 disciplinary findings for violations including 201 cruelty incidents, 24 unlawful-detention incidents, 138 ill-treatment incidents, and one torture incident; five officers were found guilty of torture in the reported judicial cases.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.4","3B.9","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The reported period ends in May 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The figures are attributed to Interior Ministry disciplinary bodies and courts.","limitations":["The source does not identify outcomes, penalties, or whether senior officials were held responsible.","The government’s figures are not independently verified."]},{"source_id":"SRC-06126ffcdef13a97","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"A September 2023 civil-society statement identified Egypt as one of the eight remaining Annex 2 states whose ratification is required for the CTBT to enter into force and stated that there had been no serious consideration of ratification by the remaining hold-out states.","question_ids":["1B.4","1B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The assessment and statement date are in September 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The statement identifies Egypt’s non-ratification but does not attribute the decision to el-Sisi personally.","limitations":["The source is an advocacy statement, not an Egyptian government record.","It does not describe Egypt’s domestic nuclear-testing posture or broader nonproliferation conduct."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8373416d1699f3ff","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"At a 29 November 2023 Security Council ministerial meeting, Egypt’s foreign minister rejected plans to transfer Palestinians from Gaza, called for a ceasefire and humanitarian action, and argued that addressing the conflict’s root causes and ending the occupation were necessary to prevent new cycles of violence.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.7","2B.10","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The statement was delivered during the target period.","ruler_attribution":"The position was stated by Egypt’s foreign minister on behalf of the Egyptian government; direct personal authorship by el-Sisi is not established.","limitations":["This is a diplomatic statement rather than evidence of a completed settlement.","The source does not show the full range of Egypt’s operational conduct in the conflict."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-637af73ad1a594c9","SRC-8e6020ebb5be6a40"],"batch_limitations":["The supplied documents vary substantially in date and evidentiary type; some describe cumulative programs or conditions extending beyond 2023.","Several sources are advocacy submissions or government self-reports, so allegations and official claims should be treated as attributed findings rather than independently adjudicated facts.","The materials provide little evidence on nuclear command-and-control, AI, cyber, biological risks, corruption, personal enrichment, electoral competition, macroeconomic budget execution, or ruler-specific appointments during 2023."]}
